inputs.share_count_basis: Average ordinary shares including potentially dilutive shares, 134,777,848, H1 FY2026 half-year report note 6 (basic weighted average 134,242,804). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and awards are settled by Employee Benefit Trust purchases rather than new issue. The count rose 113.6m -> 134.6m over FY2020-FY2025 through two acquisition-funding placings (FY2021, FY2023), which is non-SBC issuance; none is modelled forward because acquisitions are excluded from the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: share-based payments expense GBP 6.2m (cash-flow note) plus GBP 4.1m 'notional purchase of own shares on exercise of options' (financing activities; the cash cost of settling awards through the Employee Benefit Trust). No combined figure is published, so the two lines are summed. H1 FY2026: expense GBP 5.1m, EBT funding nil (plan administration change).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP (pounds); LSE quote in GBp (pence). fx_rate 100 is the fixed pounds-to-pence unit conversion, not a market rate, so it cannot go stale. Magnitude check: FY2026 adjusted EPS 255.6p against the pence quote gives a P/E in the high 20s, in line with the stock's history; no dual listing to parity-check.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T17:37:26Z (Yahoo regularMarketTime; LSE regular session close of 18 Nov 2026, not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP: 10-year gilt ~4.5% risk-free, ~5% equity risk premium, beta ~1.0 gives cost of equity ~9.5%; debt is ~4% of enterprise value (USPP fixed 4.2-5.5%), so WACC rounds to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the flows and the probability weights, not in the discount rate. Majority of earnings are USD/CAD/AUD translated to GBP; no currency premium added.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full lease payment (principal + interest; FY2025 GBP 18.5m, H1 FY2026 GBP 10.1m, ~1.15% of revenue) is charged in the flows via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (GBP 88.8m at 31 March 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt, which is the company's own covenant definition (borrowings less cash). da_pct_path is depreciation/amortisation of tangible and other intangible assets only, ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 GBP 15.0m; H1 FY2026 GBP 8.6m), so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Minority interests are immaterial (GBP 4.5m book, ~GBP 0.6m/yr profit share). Flows are consolidated; the minority is charged once through the acquisition-liabilities item in the equity bridge, which includes the put options over the remaining minority stakes (M Seals 10%, Techsil 5%).
inputs.ebitda_margin_basis: ebitda_margin_path = adjusted operating margin + 1.85pp (total depreciation and amortisation including right-of-use, FY2026 run-rate) + 0.55pp (IFRS 2 share-based payment expense, which Diploma leaves INSIDE adjusted operating profit). The engine then deducts SBC, lease cash cost and ex-ROU D&A as separate lines, so modelled EBIT sits ~0.3pp below the adjusted operating margin (lease cash exceeds right-of-use depreciation, and SBC is charged at 0.65% including EBT settlement cash). Adjusted operating profit excludes amortisation of acquisition intangibles (non-cash) and acquisition expenses (cash, ~GBP 10m/yr, belongs with the excluded acquisition spend).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US adaptations (GBP WACC, single lease treatment, GBP/GBp quote bridge). Routed as a non-US industrial operating company: value-added distributor, capital-light, modest leverage; none of the bank/REIT/holdco rows apply. First valuation of this ticker (fresh build, no reconciliation). ORGANIC-ONLY: Diploma is a buy-and-build compounder, but future acquisitions are excluded from both sides of the model - no acquired growth after FY2027 and no acquisition spend in the flows. FY2027 growth includes the ~6% from acquisitions already completed, because that cash is already in net debt. The value of future bolt-ons at ~8-9x EBIT against 20%+ returns on trading capital is therefore NOT in any scenario; this is the main reason the model sits below the market price and is a deliberate conservatism, not an oversight. TIMING GAP: FY2026 full-year results were released by RNS on 2026-11-17 but the Annual Report is not yet published, so core_metrics ends at FY2025 (annual) and H1 FY2026. FY0 is FY2026 so that year-1 is the genuinely forward year (FY2027); base_revenue GBP 1,840.3m is the RNS figure (checked against the announcement text; it is within 0.6% of filed FY2025 revenue x the filed Q3 FY2026 guidance of 14% organic + 6% acquisitions). Every ratio driver (D&A, capex, lease, SBC, tax, working capital) and last_fcf / reported_fcf are calibrated on FILED data: FY2025 annual and H1 FY2026. Net debt, debt/cash split, lease and acquisition liabilities and the diluted share count are from the filed H1 FY2026 balance sheet (31 March 2026); the move to the unaudited 30 September 2026 net debt of GBP 350.6m (FY2026 results, via the qualitative analysis; the debt/cash split is not yet available) is carried as an equity-bridge item. REFRESH all of these when the FY2026 Annual Report is parsed. Net debt at 30 September 2026 may not include acquisitions completed after year-end that are inside the '16 since the start of FY26 / GBP 368m' count; if any were, value is overstated by that spend (each GBP 10m is ~7p per share). last_fcf is FY2025 filed OCF less capex (GBP 253.2m) less SBC incl. EBT settlement (GBP 10.3m); it is after interest paid and BEFORE lease principal (GBP 14.6m), which the forward build charges separately. Company-defined FY2026 free cash flow was GBP 323.3m (94% conversion). Interest income (GBP 0.7m) not stripped: the group is in net debt. Buybacks: none; awards are settled via EBT market purchases (GBP 4.1m FY2025), so the flat count is funded. Dividends ~GBP 81m/yr are a use of the modelled flows, not a deduction.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (13.4%) is more than 30% below revenue (23.1%) and EPS (25.9%) 5-year CAGRs. All three are acquisition-driven and none is used as the forward growth rate: the model projects organic growth only (company long-run model 5%; FY2027 guidance 6%).
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 annual is the last filed full year; CAGRs run FY2022->FY2025 and FY2020->FY2025 (FY2020 is a COVID-depressed base, which flatters the 5-year figures). FCF CAGRs are on the owner series (OCF - capex - SBC - EBT settlement cash): FY2020 74.5, FY2022 104.0, FY2025 242.9. Reported-FCF CAGRs are almost identical (3-year 32.2%) because SBC is under 1% of revenue. FY2025 owner FCF is flattered by a working-capital build of only GBP 4.6m against GBP 58.9m in H1 FY2026 alone. Per-share growth is lower than these totals: shares rose 18% over the five years through two placings.

base.margin_note: Adjusted operating margin 25.5% (FY2027 guidance), fading 0.5pp a year to 24.0% by FY2030 and held; plus 2.4pp to reach the engine's EBITDA line (see inputs.ebitda_margin_basis).
base.growth_note: FY2027 12% = guidance (6% organic + 6% acquisitions already completed). Thereafter organic only: 6% for two years, easing to 3% by year 10.
base.wc_note: Negative: a stockholding distributor. Inventory + receivables - payables was GBP 353.5m at 31 March 2026, ~20% of annualised revenue; 18% of each incremental pound of revenue is assumed tied up.
base.tax_note: 25% on EBIT: the effective rate on adjusted profit (25.0% FY2025 and H1 FY2026). Cash tax paid was 24% of adjusted PBT in FY2025; the small shelter from deductible acquisition amortisation is not perpetuated.
base.capex_note: Gross capex 0.9% of revenue in FY2025 and H1 FY2026, 1.4-1.9% in FY2023-FY2024; 1.2% sits above ex-ROU D&A of 1.0% to fund organic growth.

bull.margin_note: Adjusted operating margin 26.0% in FY2027 (guidance beaten, as it was three times in FY2026), then the FY2026 record 26.5% proves durable.
bull.growth_note: FY2027 14% (8% organic + 6% acquired); organic 7-8% through FY2031 on aerospace, defence and datacentre demand, easing to 4%.

bear.margin_note: Adjusted operating margin 24.5% in FY2027, then back to 20.5% by FY2030 - the company's own '20%+' long-run model and roughly the FY2023-FY2024 level (19.7-20.9%).
bear.growth_note: FY2027 9% (3% organic + 6% acquired); flat in FY2028 as Controls laps a cyclical peak, then 2-3%.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands on guidance: 12% revenue growth (6% organic plus 6% from deals already paid for) at a 25.5% adjusted operating margin. Thereafter organic growth runs at 5-6%, slightly ahead of the company's 5% long-run model on aerospace, defence, datacentre and energy exposure in Controls, while Seals stays low-single-digit and Life Sciences recovers slowly. The margin gives back part of FY2026's 400bp jump as Peerless and the other standout Controls businesses lap exceptional comparators and mix normalises, settling at 24% - still well above the 19-22.5% of FY2022-FY2025, on the view that part of the step-up is structural mix shift toward Controls. Working capital absorbs 18p of each incremental pound of revenue. No future acquisitions on either side of the ledger.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FY2026 step-up is structural rather than a peak. Civil aerospace build-rate backlogs, defence spending and datacentre build-out keep Controls (61% of revenue) growing in the low teens, North American Seals holds high-single-digit growth and Life Sciences returns to its 4-6% norm, giving 7-8% group organic growth for five years. Operating leverage and mix hold the adjusted operating margin at the record 26.5%, with FY2027 guidance beaten as it was three times during FY2026. Acquisitions remain excluded, so this is still not the full buy-and-build bull case.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 was a cyclical and mix peak concentrated in a handful of businesses, Peerless above all (about 13% of FY2025 revenue and the main driver of the margin jump). Aerospace destocking or a datacentre capex pause takes Controls negative in FY2028 while tariff hesitancy and weak UK/European construction, agriculture and oil and gas keep Seals flat and healthcare budgets keep Life Sciences subdued. Group revenue stalls for a year and then grows 2-3%; the adjusted operating margin retraces to 20.5%, the level the group earned in FY2023-FY2024 and the floor of its own financial model. The balance sheet (0.7x leverage against a 2.0x policy and 3.5x covenants) is not a concern on this path; the damage is to earnings, not solvency. No scenario hits the terminal-value floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35, kept after considering a move both ways. Bear 15%: no refinancing, covenant or single-customer risk, and the downside is margin and growth normalisation from a record year, not survival; the concentration of the FY2026 gain in Peerless argues for more, but the base case already gives back 2.5pp of margin. Base 50%: anchored on fresh FY2027 guidance from a management team that raised guidance three times in FY2026. Bull 35%: needs only the current Controls end markets to persist, and every scenario already omits the value of future bolt-on acquisitions, which is the largest unmodelled upside.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Diploma is valued as an organic cash-flow stream: adjusted operating profit converted to unlevered owner free cash flow after share-based pay, lease payments, cash tax, capex and the working capital a growing distributor has to carry. The buy-and-build engine that has produced most of the historical growth is deliberately left out of every scenario - no acquired growth beyond deals already paid for, and no acquisition spend - so the result is a floor for the existing business rather than an estimate of the compounding machine. The gap between this value and the market price is, to a first approximation, what the market pays for future acquisitions at 8-9x EBIT plus a belief that the FY2026 margin of 26.5% is permanent. Share-based pay is under 1% of revenue, so the house and street bases sit close together and the band says little here.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin durability: the adjusted operating margin went from 22.5% to 26.5% in one year; each 1pp of terminal margin is worth roughly 4% of base value
Concentration in Peerless (aerospace fasteners) and a few Controls businesses for both growth and margin
Acquisitions are excluded: the model understates value if bolt-ons keep earning 20%+ returns, and overstates it if deal quality slips as GBP 368m a year is deployed

FY2026 balance sheet is unaudited and partly unavailable: net debt, lease and acquisition liabilities and the diluted share count come from the 31 March 2026 half-year report with a single-line roll-forward
Currency: flows are mostly USD, CAD and AUD translated to GBP; a few percent on GBP/USD moves reported profit by low-double-digit GBP millions
Working-capital intensity: the model ties up 18% of incremental revenue; H1 FY2026 absorbed GBP 58.9m as inventory was built
